subject: Post-call: Integration checklist & prompt governance for CloudOps evaluation
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.m@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@cloudops.io>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T15:12:00-05:00
Subject: Post-call: Integration checklist & prompt governance for CloudOps evaluation

Thanks again for the time today — quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have one source of truth. High level outcome: CloudOps wants a predictable path to validate Redwood for a call center summarization + internal search pilot, emphasis on security/compliance and control over prompts.

Key scoped items (agreement from call):
- SDK + auth: quick PoC using our hosted API (short-term) and a private deployment option for later. You requested Node + Python samples and a sample OAuth/JWT flow. (Owner: Dev)
- Routing & SLAs: traffic routing policy for priority live traffic, fallback to smaller model under saturation.
- Structured output / tool calling: example for ‘agent action’ output (JSON schema) to drive ops workflows.
- Embeddings + reranker: we proposed embeddings for search + a lightweight reranker to improve response precision for KB queries.
- Prompt governance: versioned prompt templates in Git, injection mitigations (input sanitization + model-side system checks), and a red‑team plan to surface problematic prompts. (Owner: Marissa + Neha)

Immediate next steps (owners & ETA):
1) Dev to share SDK quickstart + auth sample (by EOD Monday, 2026-11-08). Attachment: MAP_CloudOps_v1.xlsx includes a draft mutual action plan and target milestones.
2) Security to send SOC2 summary & address questionnaire items (Samira to confirm if the attached security_questionnaire.docx covers it).
3) Marissa/Neha to draft prompt-versioning proposal and red-team scope for the pilot (draft due 2026-11-12).
4) Schedule technical follow-up for routing and structured output schema (30–45m) — propose Wed 2026-11-10 10am PT.

Risks & open questions:
- If CloudOps requires HSM-backed keys for token signing we’ll need to confirm Private deployment timeline.
- Expected QPS for the pilot will determine batching/throughput config. Please confirm expected concurrent users.

Attaching MAP and adding links to the HubSpot deal and shared Drive. I’ll convert the MAP to a living Google sheet if that’s easier.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes | Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: MAP_CloudOps_v1.xlsx

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.m@redwood.com>, Samira Khan <samira.k@cloudops.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T17:05:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Integration checklist & prompt governance for CloudOps evaluation

Quick technical clarifications and what I’ll deliver Monday: see inline.

- SDKs: we have maintained Python and Node SDKs. Quickstart package will include: auth snippet (OAuth2 client_credentials + JWT exchange example), token refresh, and an example for streaming.
- Auth: recommended flow for hosted evaluation = API key scoped to project. For private/on-prem evaluation we support JWT signed by customer KMS; we can also integrate with your OIDC provider (Auth0/Okta). If you require HSM-backed signing, we’ll need a private deployment and add a KMS integration step to the MA P.
- Routing: runtime supports policy-based routing (latency-first vs cost-first). For the pilot we can set a hard SLO and a fallthrough to a cheaper model variant when load spikes. I’ll include an example routing.json and a suggested policy for your QPS profile.
- Structured output/tool calling: recommend a two-layer approach — 1) model returns a JSON envelope matching your actions schema; 2) runtime validates the envelope against a schema and rejects/flags mismatches. Example envelope we’ll include: {"action": "create_ticket", "params": {"summary": "..."}}. We also support function-style tool calling with explicit tool manifests.
- Embeddings/reranker: propose a two-pass flow — embeddings retrieval (FAISS/ANN index) + reranker (smaller cross-encoder). I’ll include throughput/cost estimates for 1k vs 10k docs.

Deliverables (mon):
- repo link with SDK quickstart and auth samples
- sample routing policy and routing.json
- structured-output example and schema validator note
- rough cost/throughput estimate for embeddings + reranker

If you can confirm expected pilot QPS and retention window for embeddings we’ll size the index and recommend quantization.

— Dev
Dev Patel | Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@cloudops.io>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.m@redwood.com>
Cc: Elliot Marks <elliot@cloudops.io>, CloudOps Security <security@cloudops.io>
Date: 2026-11-04T09:20:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Integration checklist & prompt governance for CloudOps evaluation

Thanks Rafael and Dev — appreciate the clear recap. A few notes from Security/Prod side: 

- I’ve attached our security questionnaire (security_questionnaire.docx). Please have the security/arch team return answers to the 40-question appendix; items about key management and data residency are high priority for us.
- We received the MAP and will review. For pilot approval we need the SOC2 summary you referenced (SOC2_summary.pdf). Can you confirm the retention window for logs and whether we can ship audit logs to our S3 bucket?
- Prompt governance: we liked the idea of versioned prompts in Git. We expect explicit change approvals for system-level prompt updates and a rollback path. Can you outline how Redwood enforces system prompts at runtime (preventing user prompt injection) and whether we can lock template versions per environment?
- Red teaming: happy to run an initial adversarial prompt test. Can Redwood provide a test harness or will you run the red-team and share findings?

Proposed next call: Tue 2026-11-09 09:00 PT — 30m to review security answers and prompt governance draft. Rafael, can you confirm?

Best,
Samira Khan
Head of Platform Engineering, CloudOps Inc.

Attachment: security_questionnaire.docx
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.m@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@cloudops.io>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T16:05:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Integration checklist & prompt governance for CloudOps evaluation

Samira — thanks, and yes, we’ll take the following approach: 

- SOC2 & logs: attaching SOC2_summary.pdf. We support streaming audit logs to your S3 (we’ll provide a signed role + delivery config). Retention window is configurable per-customer; default 90 days in hosted but can be extended on Dedicated/Private.
- Prompt enforcement: Redwood enforces system prompts at the runtime entrypoint; system templates are immutable artifacts once published to a versioned prompt registry. We also run input sanitizers (strip/escape control characters) and an optional classifier that flags high-risk inputs before execution. For pilot we recommend locking system prompt versions to the staging environment and requiring an approval step to promote to prod.
- Red-team: Redwood can run the initial red-team (we have a standard prompt-attack harness) and share vulnerability findings. Marissa will draft the red-team scope; proposed window 2026-11-16 to 2026-11-19.

I’ll schedule the Tue 2026-11-09 09:00 PT security check-in and send a calendar invite. Also looping in Legal for contract/PO next steps — can you share procurement contact? I’ll attach a DocuSign envelope for the NDA/PSA once we have names.

Next internal owners: Dev (SDK/auth/routing) | Marissa (prompt governance/red-team) | Neha (pricing + pilot sizing).

Rafael
